summary.title: Signs that you're a good programmer
summary.one_liner: A list of traits that mark a good programmer (experimentation, detachment from code, eagerness to refactor, curiosity, teaching, patience, perfectionism, platform knowledge, thinking in code), each with symptoms and advice on how to cultivate it.
takeaways: Good programmers test ideas by running code before asking others, and build that habit through side projects and low-risk experimentation.
Treat code as disposable: rewrite and delete your own work to avoid attachment to a particular design or pattern.
Refactor for clarity, reuse of platform features, and removal of dead code, in a rough order of importance listed by the author.
Growth comes from struggling with hard problems, writing about them, and reflecting on the solutions.
Teaching others is a way to improve your own understanding; the author recommends practicing on non-programming subjects.
summary.summary: This is a personal essay by a software developer, written as the counterpart to his popular 'Signs you're a bad programmer' article. It is organized into numbered traits, each with a list of symptoms and a section titled 'How to acquire this trait' that gives practical, often anecdotal advice. The author mixes humour, references to other programmers and examples such as an integer-type bug story. Some points are opinion-based, and the page itself notes that a few are counterproductive.
